text:
Vancouver scored first and then watched New Jersey's power play take the game away. The Devils cashed three of their four man-advantage chances, and all four of their goals after Linus Karlsson's early strike came from Nico Hischier, Jesper Bratt and Jesper Boqvist. Hischier scored twice on the power play, the second a snap shot with 10 seconds left in the second period that made it 4-1 and ended any real doubt.

The scoreboard wasn't far off the play. New Jersey generated 4.01 expected goals to Vancouver's 2.35, and outshot the Canucks 37-21 with a 64-42 edge in shot attempts. Most of that gap came on the power play: at even strength the chance quality was closer, 2.68 to 2.06. Still, the Devils won the expected-goals count in all three periods, and in a simulated replay of every shot they take the game 76 percent of the time. Vancouver's 3 goals-against on 34 shots on Leevi Meriläinen were roughly what the chances warranted.

Jake Allen made the difference at the other end, stopping 20 of 21 against 2.35 expected goals for a save total 1.35 goals better than expected. Jake DeBrusk was Vancouver's most dangerous skater, putting seven shots on net (0.94 expected goals) and assisting on the opener, but he never got a second goal. Bratt added a goal and an assist, and Jack Hughes set up two scores, including the one that sent Hischier into the break with a three-goal cushion.
